# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 4

**4:1** And behold, an angel of the Lord appeared before her, saying: "Anna, Anna, the Lord God has heard your prayer. You shall conceive and give birth, and your offspring shall be spoken of throughout all the world."

**4:2** And Anna said, "As the Lord God lives, whether I bear a son or a daughter, I will bring the child as an offering to the Lord my God, and it shall minister before him all the days of its life."

**4:3** And behold, two messengers came to her, saying: "Behold, Joachim your husband is coming with his flocks." For an angel of the Lord had appeared to Joachim, saying: "Joachim, Joachim, the Lord God has heard your prayer. Go down from here, for your wife Anna has conceived in her womb."

**4:4** And Joachim went down at once and called his shepherds, saying: "Bring me ten she-lambs without blemish for the Lord my God; bring me twelve calves for the priests and the elders; and bring me a hundred male goats for all the people."

**4:5** And Joachim came with his flocks, and Anna stood at the gate. She saw him coming and ran and hung upon his neck, saying: "Now I know that the Lord God has greatly blessed me. For behold, the widow is no longer a widow, and she who was childless shall conceive."

**4:6** And Joachim rested the first day in his house.

---

## Translator's Note

The angelic double annunciation (to Anna in the garden, to Joachim in the wilderness) is modeled closely on the annunciation pattern in the Hebrew Bible. Anna's vow in 4:2 is the crucial narrative hinge: the child will not be an ordinary child, but a temple-dedicated nazirite from birth — exactly as Hannah dedicated Samuel. The return reunion scene (4:5) echoes both Ruth 1 and Jacob's homecoming.
